what_it_does: This paper measures performance of cloud-based supercomputers—Azure Eagle (14,400 H100 GPUs, ranked 3rd fastest in the world) and Azure Reindeer (960 H200 GPUs, ranked 32nd)—to understand how well they perform compared to traditional on-premises supercomputers. The researchers run standardized benchmarks (small synthetic workloads testing individual operations) and full scientific simulations to measure computational speed, communication speed between nodes, network latency (delay in data transfer), and the overhead cost of cloud virtualization (running in virtual machines rather than bare metal). This work reveals whether cloud supercomputers can match or exceed dedicated on-premises systems for high-performance computing workloads.
